anomalies.observed: The USB-C D+ pins and the ESP32-C3 USB_D+/GPIO19 pin are all placed on the GND net: J12 pin A6 (D+), J12 pin B6 (D+), and U1 pin 27 (GPIO19/USB_D+) appear as nodes on net GND. Meanwhile the D- pins and U1 pin 26 (GPIO18/USB_D-) are connected together on /Microcontroller/USB_D-. There is no separate USB_D+ net.
anomalies.expected: If the USB-C connector is used for programming/data, the D+ pins of J12 and U1 pin 27 should form a USB_D+ net, not be shorted to GND. Even if USB data were intentionally unused, shorting only D+ to GND while leaving D- connected to the MCU is not a standard or benign USB-C sink configuration.
anomalies.impact: USB data enumeration and USB-based programming will not work because USB D+ is shorted to ground; the differential USB pair is asymmetrically terminated and violates normal USB-C sink/data wiring expectations.

parsed.summary: The main deviation is that USB D+ (J12 A6/B6 and U1 pin 27) is shorted to GND while USB D- is connected to the MCU, which would prevent normal USB data/programming behavior and is not documented as a known limitation.
